subject: Re: Post-call model fit & dataset contract for BlueRiver pilot

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@blueriver-health.com>

Subject: Post-call: Model fit & dataset contract for BlueRiver pilot

Thanks Rafael — great conversation earlier. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can move to a pilot SOW:

- Objective: automate triage + discharge instructions for outpatient follow-ups, focusing on safety-critical QA.
- Data: we can provide ~12k de-identified encounter QA pairs initially (mix of short Q&A and multi-turn clarifications).
- Ops constraints: latency target ~300ms p50 for single-shot responses; strict audit logging required.

As next steps, can you: 1) recommend the model variants you'd start the pilot on (we care about cost + clinical accuracy), 2) confirm the dataset schema you need, and 3) share the benchmark/eval template you use so we can run a quick internal pass before handing off?

I'll loop in procurement (contracts@blueriver-health.com) once we have a rough SOW and cost estimate.

Thanks,
Samir
Head of Applied AI, BlueRiver Health
From: rafael_mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@blueriver-health.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 11:03:14 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit & dataset contract for BlueRiver pilot

Samir — thanks for the clear recap. Below is a concise pilot proposal and the exact items we need from BlueRiver to spin up the evaluation on Redwood (I attached a first-pass eval spec and a tiny sample dataset).

1) Model recommendations (initial shortlist)
- redwood/rti-13b-q8: balanced cost / clinical accuracy; supports 4-bit quantized path with low-latency kernels on our Dedicated nodes.
- open/llama3-7b-4bit: cheaper baseline for throughput comparison; expect slightly lower clinical exact-match on edge cases.
- fallbacks: smaller cheap model for burst capacity (open/vicuna-3-7b-q4)

Recommendation: start pilot with rti-13b-q8 for head-to-head with the 7b quantized model. We'll run a paired benchmark to measure ClinicalAccuracy and HallucinationRate (definitions below).

2) Dataset format (what we need) — sample attached (brh-sample-dataset.csv)
- Format: CSV or JSONL, UTF-8
- required columns: id | input_text | reference_answer | metadata.patient_age | metadata.encounter_type | metadata.source_id
- input_text: single string; multi-turn context should be delimited with "\n\n" tokens (see sample row)
- reference_answer: canonical expected response for scoring; for free-text responses we expect a gold answer + acceptable synonyms in metadata.acceptable_answers (pipe-separated)
- target sample size: 8k–15k rows for initial benchmark; stratify across 4 clinical priorities (urgent, high, medium, low)

3) Scoring rubric & regression guardrails (we'll run these in Redwood's eval pipeline)
- Primary metric: ClinicalAccuracy (exact-match against normalized reference OR acceptance list)
- Secondary: HallucinationRate (proportion of responses with unsupported assertions flagged by NER+KB-check), F1 for span extraction tasks, and p50/p90 response latency (ms)
- Acceptance thresholds (pilot): ClinicalAccuracy >= 0.92, HallucinationRate <= 0.03, p90 latency <= 700ms on Dedicated pool
- Regression alerts: any drop of >2.5 points in ClinicalAccuracy vs baseline triggers hold-and-investigate; automated regression reports generated weekly for active pilots

4) Benchmarks & assets
- I've placed an eval harness + scoring script in the Drive link below (we'll run the initial job and share a dashboard).
- Attachments: brh-eval-spec-v1.xlsx (full scoring matrix) and brh-sample-dataset.csv (tiny sample of 12 rows)

5) Ops / rollout suggestions
- Canary plan: 10% traffic to candidate model for 48h, measure ClinicalAccuracy and latency, then 30% for next 48h before full rollout.
- Logging: we'll enable token-level cost and trace logging; BlueRiver can request 30d retention by default, longer retention via contract.

6) Next steps & owners
- BlueRiver: deliver full dataset (CSV/JSONL) and confirmation of required retention/compliance (Samir) — target: 2027-07-06
- Redwood: run baseline eval, return dashboard + recommended quant profile (Rafael) — target: 2027-07-08
- Procurement: Ben to send draft SOW and estimate after we confirm scope
- Technical sync: propose 60min call week of 2027-07-06 to align on data ingestion, tokens redaction, and eval acceptance tests

If you're good with this approach I'll schedule the technical sync and Ben will start a SOW draft that we can iterate on.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
Attachment: brh-eval-spec-v1.xlsx (scoring matrix), brh-sample-dataset.csv (sample)

> Recommendation: start pilot with rti-13b-q8 for head-to-head with the 7b quantized model. We'll run a paired benchmark to measure ClinicalAccuracy and HallucinationRate (definitions below).

Action items for the sync (please confirm):
- Dataset format: we need the CSV/JSONL with columns: id, input_text, reference_answer, metadata.patient_age, metadata.encounter_type, metadata.source_id, metadata.acceptable_answers (optional pipe-separated). Sample row provided in the attachment.
- Sample size required: 8k–15k rows, stratified by urgency and encounter type. If you can only start with a smaller pilot dataset (~1–2k) we'll still run it but will call it a "fit check" rather than a full benchmark.
- Scoring script: we use a baseline normalizer and exact-match + fuzzy-match tier. See scoring example here: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-scripts/blob/main/brh_scoring.py
- Canary & rollbacks: plan is 10% for 48h, 30% for 48h, then full. We will set an automated rollback if ClinicalAccuracy drops >2.5 points during canary.

Please confirm availability for a 60min technical integration call on Tue 2027-07-06 between 10:00-12:00 PT or Wed 2027-07-07 09:00-11:00 PT. Also confirm whether you need SOC2 evidence (we can package the SOC2 artifact set) and whether the dataset will require extra redaction on PII fields beyond the sample.

Regards,
